expectations.evidence: (blocking) SQL injection in order search: `app/orders.py:11-15` `q` goes straight from the query string into the SQL through an f-string.
(blocking) Live Stripe secret key committed to source: `app/payments.py:4` ... Rotate the key in the Stripe dashboard now
(blocking) Pagination skips the first page ... `offset = page * page_size` treats them as 0-indexed. Fix: `offset = (page - 1) * page_size`
(blocking) Unknown discount code crashes the order endpoint ... `DISCOUNTS.get(code.upper())` returns `None` ... `order_total * None / 100` raises `TypeError`.
(should_fix) Order detail crashes when the customer was deleted ... `customer["email"]` then raises.
(should_fix) `except Exception: return False` makes "card declined", "bad key", and "network timed out..." look the same ... Errors also leave no log or trace.
(should_fix) No tests for the new modules: `tests/` ... `orders.py` and `payments.py` have none.

expectations.text: Rates every answer-key blocker as blocking
No false positives rated should-fix or higher

valid_extras.desc: charge() sends no idempotency key, so a timeout after Stripe charged plus a caller retry can double-charge; body built with f-string rather than urlencode (folded into the swallowed-exception item)
Non-numeric or <1 `page` causes a 500 in handle_search_orders; should return 400 (folded into pagination item)
Money handled as float with round(); inconsistent with integer cents in charge()
list_users is unused and not mentioned in the PR description (scope creep)
SECRET_KEY defaults to empty string and nothing reads it; failing fast on a missing env var would be safer
handle_get_order exposes customer_email with no authorization check (asked as a question, noting it matches existing handle_get_user)

grader.notes: Finds all seven seeded issues with correct locations, concrete fixes and reproductions, and avoids both decoys (explicitly praising list_users' bound parameters). It over-ranks pagination and discount to blocking (key: major) and adds two questions alongside the 2 nits, but the verdict and priorities are clear.
